title: The Impact of Renewable Energy and Regulatory Quality on Sustainable Competitiveness: A Panel Data Analysis
content:
ABSTRACT

This paper analyzed the interplay between renewable energy, regulatory quality, and sustainable competitiveness across 172 countries from 2012 to 2023. Utilizing robust econometric techniques, including pooled OLS, random effects, DKSE, system GMM, and panel quantile regression, it provides novel insights into the roles of renewable energy and regulatory quality in shaping sustainable competitiveness. Results reveal that renewable energy and regulatory quality significantly enhance sustainable competitiveness, with higher renenwable energy shares and strong regulations amplifying competitiveness. Critically, regulatory quality moderates the renewable energy-competitiveness nexus, with stronger institutions magnifying the benefits of clean energy deployment. This synergy persists across the conditional distribution of competitiveness, from the 25th to 90th percentiles. Notably, these results indicate that the benefits of stronger regulatory quality for sustainable competitiveness extend across countries at different levels of competitiveness, including those at the lower end of the distribution. These highlight the need for integrated frameworks that bridge environmental sustainability, governance, and economic performance.
